questions.cardText:
[Physics] Which one of the following is the hottest?
A. A lightning bolt
B. The Sun’s surface
C. The Earth’s core
Answer: A. A lightning bolt can reach temperatures of up to about 50,000 °F (about 27,000 °C). In contrast, the surface of the Sun and the Earth’s core are both around 10,000 °F (about 5,537 °C). However, the Sun’s core is far hotter, with temperatures reaching approximately 27,000,000 °F (about 15,000,000 °C).
questions.de: Welche Temperatur kann die Luft in einem Blitzkanal ungefähr erreichen – ein Vielfaches der Temperatur der Sonnenoberfläche?
questions.en: Roughly what temperature can the air in a lightning bolt reach — several times hotter than the surface of the Sun?

timeline.labelEn: Benjamin Franklin proposes the kite experiment, showing that lightning is electricity
timeline.labelDe: Benjamin Franklin schlägt das Drachenexperiment vor, das zeigt, dass Blitze elektrischer Natur sind

questions.notes: Comparative MC turned into the underlying fact. Wikipedia/NOAA: the air heats to about 30,000 °C; return-stroke plasma may exceed 50,000 °F (~27,800 °C) — the card's ~27,000 °C is in the same range. Accept roughly 27,000–30,000 °C.

questions.cardText:
[Earth Science] Which of the following holds the most of the world’s freshwater?
A. Atmosphere
B. Lakes and rivers
C. Glaciers and ice caps
Answer: C. Glaciers and ice caps hold about 70% of the world’s freshwater.
questions.de: Wo ist der größte Teil des Süßwassers der Erde gespeichert – etwa 70 Prozent davon?
questions.en: Where is most of the world's freshwater stored — about 70% of it?

timeline.labelEn: Peter Gleick's 'Water in Crisis' publishes the classic estimate of Earth's water distribution
timeline.labelDe: Peter Gleicks „Water in Crisis“ veröffentlicht die klassische Schätzung der Wasserverteilung der Erde

questions.notes: Wikipedia table (after Gleick 1993): glaciers and permanent snow hold 68.7% of fresh water (ice and snow total 69.6%).
